titleEn: Look in Their Eyes and Say Sorry!

pages.text: Crash! Digging for roots, Tumba struck a small acacia beside them. Snap! A branch fell. "Oh... What do I do?" Tumba stopped dead.
Nia lowered their neck to the broken branch. Their ears flattened. "I saved this tree's leaves, eating one each day..." Tumba's face burned. They wanted to apologize, but shame kept their snout shut.
Tumba quietly turned away. Alone, Nia picked up the broken branch with their mouth. A dry wind blew between them. The shore grew strangely quiet.
Moya saw Tumba's unhappy face. "Your heart feels heavy?" Moya lay beside Tumba. "It's okay. What could help?" Tumba thought quietly.
Not apologizing felt like a huge stone on Tumba's chest—heavy, tight, and poking. "What do I do?" Moya said, "Look straight into Nia's eyes and say sorry."
Then Nia approached softly. "Tumba... I really want to play together." Nia's heart had been heavy, too. Tumba's heart thumped. Nia had come first.
Tumba planted all four feet, gathered courage, and breathed deeply. Nia lowered their eyes to Tumba's. "Nia, I'm sorry I broke your tree." Look in their eyes and say sorry!
The heavy stone seemed to melt away. Tumba's tail popped up. Nia smiled. "It's okay! I wanted us to play together, too."

Days later, they stood beside the tree. Nia pointed with their muzzle. "A new shoot beside the break!" A pale green leaf poked out. Tumba promised, "One, don't turn away after a mistake! Two, look in their eyes! Three, say sorry!"

Moya leaned against them. "Knowing how to say sorry is wonderful, Tumba!" Nia nuzzled Tumba's back. Even through embarrassment, looking and saying sorry made their heart light. Look in their eyes and say sorry!
